messages.subject: Trouble using gdbsource on linux
parts:
Hi there.
I still don't know how to use gdbsource() with my code. I followed the instructions on debug_tutorial but my results are kind of different. After running gdbsource(codeR,interactive=TRUE) I get the Current Output (Below), and when I hit Enter a couple of times nothing happens. So, I don't know how to do it (when I openned via command line, it worked).

Reproducible Steps:

My poisson_bivariate.cpp code:
// Bivariate Poisson with random effects correlated
#include <TMB.hpp>
#include "debug_print.hpp"

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  DATA_MATRIX(Y);         // 2 Response variables (or more) n x 2
  DATA_MATRIX(X);         // Same Covariates for both random effects
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(Beta1); // FIXED EFFECTS PARAMETER 1
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(Beta2); // FIXED EFFECTS PARAMETER 2
  PARAMETER_MATRIX(U);    // Random effects n x 2
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(sigmas);
  PARAMETER(rho);
  int n = Y.size();
  Type nll = 0;
  // Mean Structure
  vector<Type> eta1(n);
  vector<Type> eta2(n);
  vector<Type> u0(n);
  u0 = U.col(0);
  vector<Type> u1(n);
  u1 = U.col(1);
  eta1 = exp(X*Beta1 + vector<Type>(U.col(0)));
  eta2 = exp(X*Beta2 + vector<Type>(U.col(1)));
  REPORT(eta1);
  REPORT(eta2);
  nll = -sum(dpois(vector<Type>(Y.col(0)), eta1, true));
  nll -= sum(dpois(vector<Type>(Y.col(1)), eta2, true));
  // Reparametrization
  int k = sigmas.size();
  REPORT(k);
  for (int j = 0; j<k; j++){
    sigmas(j) = pow(exp(sigmas(j)), 2);
  }
  rho = -1 + 2*(exp(rho)/(exp(rho) + 1));
  Type cov_rho = rho*sqrt(sigmas(0))*sqrt(sigmas(1));
  // // Normal Multivariada
  vector<Type> rho_temp(1);
  rho_temp(0) = cov_rho;
  using namespace density;

  for (int i=0;  i<n; i++){
    nll += VECSCALE(UNSTRUCTURED_CORR(rho_temp),sigmas)(U.row(i));
  }

  return nll;
}


My poisson_bivariate.R code:
library(TMB)
setwd("~/Google Drive/Mestrado/dissertacao/TMB/MultivariateModels")
model <- "poisson_bivariate" #1st try
compile(paste0(model, ".cpp"))
dyn.load(dynlib(model))
# Data
counts <- c(18,17,15,20,10,20,25,13,12)
outcome <- gl(3,1,9)
treatment <- gl(3,3)
d.AD <- data.frame(treatment, outcome, counts)
set.seed(190)
d.AD$counts2 <- d.AD$counts + rpois(nrow(d.AD), 3)
Rinterface(paste0(model, ".cpp"))
n <- nrow(d.AD)
data <- list(Y = as.matrix(d.AD[, 3:4]),
             X = model.matrix(~ outcome + treatment, d.AD))
params <- list(Beta1 = rep(0, 5),
               Beta2 = rep(0, 5)
               ,U = matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = 2),
               sigmas = c(1, 1),
               rho = .3
)
obj <- MakeADFun(data = data,
                 parameters = params,
                 DLL = model,
                 method = "BFGS",
                 hessian = T,
                 silent = F
                 ,random = c("U"))
(it crashes my session after calling MakeADFun)

My auxiliar code:
library(TMB)
setwd("~/Google Drive/Mestrado/dissertacao/TMB/MultivariateModels")
code <- "poisson_bivariate"
codeR <- paste0(code, ".R")
# source(codeR)
gdbsource(codeR,interactive=TRUE)

And I get:

Current Output: (hit Enter and nothing happens)


And after that, I need to kill it (commands like backtrace, print don't work).

Expected Output (As in the case studies):

TMB Version: 1.7.16
R Version: R version 3.6.3 (2020-02-29)
Operating System: Linux 18.04
Obs: I noticed that the debug tutorial runs on a Windows Machine (but I don't know how it would change to mine)

Tks in advance

Hi,

The first recommendation from skimming over the code is to suggest adding debugging flags to the compile call in poisson_bivariate.R

compile(paste0(model, ".cpp"), flags = "g")  
or 
compile(paste0(model, ".cpp"), flags = "g1")  

Depending on the compiler, in C++ you can get different 'levels' of debugging information with different flags i.e.  "g1"  vs "g" see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10475040/gcc-g-vs-g3-gdb-flag-what-is-the-difference

parts:
I find gdbsource to be the best method for locating C++ errors like this one. I usually don't have the best knowledge 
to decipher what the error is from looking at the gdb output. But I find 90% of my debugging is just locating where the 
the errors are, and most of the time they are simple implementation error.

The output from gdb tells you the issue is at line 44. See the point #4 in second screen shot you shared. So there seems to 
be an error at the line
nll += VECSCALE(UNSTRUCTURED_CORR(rho_temp),sigmas)(U.row(i)); 

So I would recommend looking at the documentation for this https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/classdensity_1_1UNSTRUCTURED__CORR__t.html

There are some other issues in the code though, you specify a parameter called 'rho', and then you overwrite that parameter at line 35 below
rho = -1 + 2*(exp(rho)/(exp(rho) + 1));

You probably shouldn't do that, as I imagine the Auto-differentiation will not be happy, but others will know more than me on this. Perhaps rename your PARAMETER(transformed_rho); 
Type rho = -1 + 2*(exp( transformed_rho )/(exp( transformed_rho ) + 1));
